en.intro_paragraph: Carats is a full-stack JavaScript framework that provides a modern development experience without relying on React. It uses JJSX for building user interfaces and supports both server-side and client-side rendering.
en.installation_intro: Learn how to set up a Carats project from scratch.
en.installation_requirements_content: Before you begin, make sure you have Bun installed on your system. Carats uses Bun for package management and running the development server.
en.installation_step2: Initialize a new project with Bun
en.installation_tsconfig_desc: Carats requires a proper tsconfig.json at the root of your project with specific compiler options to support JJSX.
en.tsconfig_desc: Carats requires a proper tsconfig.json at the root of your project with specific compiler options to support JJSX.
en.package_desc: Add the following scripts to your package.json to enable development and build commands.
en.structure_desc: A typical Carats project has the following structure:
en.props_desc: Props are passed to components as expected, and children are contained within the component tags.
en.head_desc: Components can provide dynamic head tags (title, meta) by assigning to this.head in the component function.
en.attributes_desc: HTML attributes are preserved as-is. Unlike React, you cannot pass arrow functions to event handlers like onclick. Use addEventListener inside the hydrate callback for event handling.
en.entrypoint_desc: The server entrypoint is defined in src\server\entrypoint.ts using defineServerEntry from @carats/ssr. It handles rendering and culet registration.
en.core_concepts_intro: Understanding the core concepts of Carats will help you build applications more effectively.
en.jjsx_desc: JJSX enables a pure HTML & JavaScript experience similar to PHP. It allows you to write JavaScript code inside TSX/JSX files similar to React, but without React hooks or React DOM.
en.facets_desc: Facets are the routing system in Carats. They define the routes and page components of your application. Facets are defined in src\client\facets.cara.ts and can include parameters, suspense states, and in-app routing configuration.
en.culets_desc: Culets are server-side functions that provide data to components. They are defined in src\server\culets and seated in the server entrypoint. Components that need server-side data are 'burnished' to automatically fetch from their culet.
en.server_props_desc: Server props are data fetched from culets on the server and passed to components. Burnished components automatically receive this data without manual fetching.
en.server_props_auto_text: Server props are automatically passed to burnished components:
en.components_intro: Carats components are similar to React components but with some key differences in how they handle attributes and events.
en.component_structure_desc: Components are .tsx files that export a default function. They can have props, defaultProps, and children.
en.component_props_desc: Props are passed to components as expected, and children are contained within the component tags.
en.component_head_desc: Components can provide dynamic head tags (title, meta) by assigning to this.head in the component function.
en.component_attributes_desc: HTML attributes are preserved as-is. Unlike React, you cannot pass arrow functions to event handlers like onclick. Use addEventListener inside the hydrate callback for event handling.
en.burnish_desc: Burnished components automatically fetch data from their culet. Wrap your component with the Burnish function from @carats/render to enable this feature.
en.burnish_recast: Use the recast option to fetch fresh data on every render instead of caching.
en.server_side_intro: Carats provides automatic server-side rendering (SSR) through its @carats/ssr package.
en.server_entrypoint_desc: The server entrypoint is defined in src\server\entrypoint.ts using defineServerEntry from @carats/ssr. It handles rendering and culet registration.
en.culets_server_desc: Culets are defined using the culet function from @carats/ssr. They should only be defined if a server-side prop is needed for a route.
en.culet_seat_desc: External culets must be seated using the seat function before they can be used.
en.express_integration_desc: Carats can be integrated with Express using @carats/express. The carats middleware is used to handle Carats routes.
en.hooks_intro: Carats provides hooks for state management and client-side hydration through the @carats/hooks package.
en.use_hook_desc: The use() hook provides state management. Unlike React hooks, it is not reactive, so DOM updates must be handled manually.
en.use_interface: The use() function returns a State object with get, set, and subscribe methods.
en.hydrate_desc: The hydrate() callback runs only on the client side after the load event is dispatched. Use it to access DOM elements created by the same component.
en.onmount_desc: The onMount() callback runs immediately on the client side. Use it when you don't need to access DOM elements.
en.clear_hydrations_desc: Clears all registered hydration callbacks. Useful for cleanup in tests or specific scenarios.
en.styling_intro: Carats uses scoped SASS for styling, promoting semantic HTML with minimal CSS classes.
en.base_sass_desc: The base.sass file in src/client contains global design tokens and style resets. All other SASS files should import it using @use with 'as *'.
en.design_tokens_desc: Define colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints, and other design tokens at the top level of base.sass. Avoid nesting.
en.semantic_html_desc: Prefer semantic HTML elements with minimal class usage. Let the component structure and design tokens handle styling.
en.best_practices_intro: Follow these best practices for maintainable styling:
en.best_practice1: Define tokens at top level - Don't nest design tokens in mixins or functions
en.best_practice2: Use semantic HTML - Let the structure define the styling, not classes
en.best_practice3: Import base.sass correctly - Always use `@use 'path/to/base.sass' as *`
en.best_practice4: Keep specificity low - Avoid deeply nested selectors
en.best_practice5: Use variables for consistency - Never hardcode colors, spacing, or sizes
